opus-5.5.text:
Thanks for having me. The way I think about it, Mosaic was always about helping companies build their own models on their own data, but training a model is only one piece of the puzzle. Before you train anything, you need your data clean, organized, governed, and accessible. After you train it, you need to deploy it, monitor it, connect it to the rest of your systems, and make sure the right people have access to it. At Mosaic we were very good at the training part, and we had to tell customers, "Go figure out the rest and come back to us."

Databricks fills in the rest. So many enterprises already keep their data there, so the hardest part, getting the data, is suddenly much easier. Instead of shipping terabytes somewhere else and worrying about security and compliance, you can build models right where the data already lives, under the governance you already have. That changes the conversation completely. It's no longer "Should we take on this big science project?" It's "We have the data, we have the platform, let's try it."

It also widens what we can offer. Not every problem needs a model trained from scratch. Sometimes fine-tuning is the right answer, sometimes retrieval, sometimes a well-designed system built around an existing model, and sometimes a smaller, cheaper model will do the job better than a giant one. Being part of a larger platform lets us meet customers wherever they are on that spectrum, rather than only selling the one thing we're best at.

And on the research side, it's a huge opportunity. We get to see real enterprise problems at enormous scale, which keeps us honest about what actually matters. Benchmarks are nice, but what customers need is for these models to work reliably on their specific tasks, at a cost that makes sense. Having the resources and the customer base to study that problem seriously is very exciting to me.

r001.rationale: The response says Databricks makes enterprise data easier to access and lets Mosaic build models where that data lives, but it never identifies those models as large language models.

r002.rationale: The response mentions Databricks’ platform and customer base, but does not identify an established enterprise sales channel as a way to expand Mosaic’s commercial reach.

fable-5.1.text:
Thanks for having me. The short version is that Databricks gives us two things Mosaic never had on its own: data and distribution.

Mosaic's whole thesis was that any company should be able to train or fine-tune its own models efficiently. We got pretty good at the efficiency part, the training stack, the hardware utilization, the recipes. But the hard part for a business was never really the GPUs. It was that their data was sitting in a thousand places, governed by a dozen different access rules, and nobody knew how to get it into a shape a model could learn from. Databricks has spent a decade solving exactly that problem. So now the model-training piece can plug directly into where the data already lives, with the governance already in place. That's a much shorter path from "we have an idea" to "we have a model in production."

The second thing is reach. Mosaic had a great set of customers, but they were the ones motivated enough to come find us. Databricks has many thousands of companies already on the platform, and most of them aren't going to hire a research team. For them, building a custom model needs to feel about as hard as running a SQL query. That's the bar we're trying to hit, and it changes how we think about the tools we build. Less "here's a training framework," more "point it at your data and tell it what you want."

And honestly, it changes the research agenda too. When you're close to real customers with real data, you learn fast which problems actually matter. Things like retrieval, evaluation, and getting good results out of smaller models on domain-specific data turn out to be where most of the value is, not just squeezing another few points on a benchmark. Being inside Databricks keeps us honest about that.

r001.rationale: The response says Databricks connects Mosaic’s training tools to business data where it already lives, with governance in place, enabling companies to build models.

r002.rationale: It says Databricks brings Mosaic reach to many thousands of companies already on its platform, expanding beyond customers who would seek Mosaic out themselves.

astra-6.text:
I think the biggest thing is that Databricks brings us much closer to where businesses actually have their data and do their work. At Mosaic, we were focused on making it easier and more efficient to train models. But for a business, training a model is one piece of a much bigger problem: How do I use my data, build something useful, evaluate it, and get it into production?

With Databricks, we have an opportunity to connect those pieces. Instead of asking a company to assemble an entire infrastructure stack before it can even experiment, we can help make building and using custom models part of the workflow it already has. And that lets us focus on the outcome: a model that does a particular job well for that business, at a cost that makes sense.

r001.rationale: It connects Databricks to businesses’ data and custom models, but does not clearly identify access to enterprise data stores as enabling businesses to use large language models.

r002.rationale: It does not mention Databricks’ established enterprise sales channel or its role in expanding Mosaic’s commercial reach.

sol-6.1.text:
I think the biggest thing is that Databricks brings us much closer to the data and to the customers who want to use it. At Mosaic, we focused on making it easier to train and customize models. But for a business, the model is only one piece. You also need to bring your data together, manage access to it, evaluate whether the model is doing something useful, and get it into production.

Putting those pieces together creates an opportunity to make customization much more accessible. A company can build something around its own data and its own needs, with that work happening alongside the infrastructure it already uses. That’s what excites me: taking the capabilities we developed at Mosaic and making them useful to a much broader set of businesses.

r001.rationale: The response says Databricks brings Mosaic closer to business data, supports bringing data together and managing access, and enables companies to customize models around their own data.

r002.rationale: It mentions reaching more businesses and being closer to customers, but does not identify Databricks’ established enterprise sales channel as the means of expanding commercial reach.
